title: Styles and selectors
cards/0/title: The selector picks, the setter changes
cards/0/body: An Avalonia style looks a lot like a CSS rule: the selector says which elements it applies to, and the setters say what to change.
cards/0/code:
<Style Selector="Button.primary">
  <Setter Property="Background" Value="#4f7cff"/>
  <Setter Property="Foreground" Value="White"/>
</Style>

<Button Classes="primary" Content="Save"/>
cards/1/body:
Button: by type.
.primary: by class (Classes="primary").
#Save: by name (x:Name="Save").
StackPanel Button: a button anywhere inside a StackPanel.
StackPanel > Button: direct children only.
cards/2/task: Select every button in the window.
cards/3/task: Only the buttons sitting directly in the toolbar (not inside the Border).
cards/4/task: All buttons inside the toolbar, at any depth.
cards/6/body: Element states use a colon: :pointerover (the mouse is over the element), :pressed, :disabled, :focus.
cards/6/deep: Why /template/ ContentPresenter? The Fluent theme paints the hover background on an inner element of the button's template. A style on the button itself loses, so you need to target the same part of the template.
cards/7/q: How does "StackPanel Button" differ from "StackPanel > Button"?
cards/7/options/0: The first matches buttons at any depth inside, the second only direct children
cards/7/explain: Just like CSS: a space means descendant, > means child.
cards/8/q: Match each selector to what it selects
cards/9/q: Which selectors match <Button Classes="primary danger"/>? Select all that apply.
cards/9/explain: Several classes in a row means the element must have all of them. The button has no warning class.
cards/10/q: Give the button the Button.danger style
cards/10/explain: The Classes property is a space-separated list of classes.
